before: Barclays Bank Account has been blocked since the switch, except for paying off what it owes.
after: Barclays Bank Account is blocked, so nothing was moved. It was overdrawn when you switched banks, and it stays blocked until the overdraft is paid off. Move money into it to clear what it owes, and it closes once it’s repaid.
why: The reference's example 4: what happened, why, and the way out. Its 'Nothing was moved.' became a clause, since a sentence opening on Nothing is over the tics budget.
verified: lending.ts sets switchDebt only when the old account was overdrawn on the switch day, and closes it once its balance is back to zero; moving money in is allowed. Decision 4's bank.switch: words only.

before: Chase Total Checking has only $40.50, so nothing was moved.
after: Chase Total Checking has only $40.50 available, so nothing was moved.
why: The figure is the available balance, pending card payments already off it, and the word says so (the reference's banking restriction).
verified: bank.transfer compares with from.balance; systems/pending.ts: postedBalance = balance − pendingOn. tests/language-money.test.ts.

before: You can take €2,000 more out of Flexgeld this month without notice. More than that takes three months’ notice.
after: You can take only €1,999.50 more out of Flexgeld this month without notice, so nothing was moved. To take out more, you’d have to close the account, which takes three months’ notice.
why: The figure was rounded up past the limit (defect m1), the refusal didn't say nothing moved, and notice can only be given by closing the account.
verified: tests/editorial-money.test.ts m1, failing without the fix; bank.close_savings is the only command that schedules SAVINGS_NOTICE_KIND.

before: It’s your only current account. Open another one first: you always need a current account to be paid into.
after: It’s your only checking account, and you always need one for your wages to be paid into. Open another one first.
why: Checking account, the glossary's word; the reason first, then the step.
verified: tests/evidence-g14-money.test.ts and four other tests assert it on bank.close_current.

before: Its fees, €0.16, are more than it holds. Pay in €0.06 first.
after: Its fees, €0.16, are more than it holds. Move €0.06 into it first.

before: Your €2,500.00 payment to AktivKonto didn’t go. There wasn’t enough in Flexgeld on the day.
after: Your €2,500.00 payment to AktivKonto didn’t go through: there wasn’t enough available in Flexgeld that day. You can set it up again under How You Pay.

before: Closing it now charges its fees to the day, €3.12 ($3.39): October’s €6.90 for the 14 days of its 31 it’s been open, €3.12. German law charges a month’s fee only to the day an account closes.
after: Closing it now charges €3.12 ($3.39) in fees: €3.12 of October’s €6.90 fee, for the 14 days of its 31 the account has been open. Under German law, a month’s fee is charged only up to the day an account closes.
why: The total first, then what makes it up, the share before the fee it's a share of; the law said as the bank's rule.
verified: closingFeesDue's figures unchanged; tests/remaining-09-banking.test.ts renders every variant.

before: Closing it now charges €4.90 ($5.33), the €4.90 for last month, due on the 1st: October’s was counted at the month’s end.
after: Closing it now charges €4.90 ($5.33): the €4.90 for October, which would come off on the 1st. October’s fee was already counted at the month’s end.
why: At 11:30 PM on October 31 the fee due on the 1st is October's, not last month's.
verified: ING's feesDue holds a fee only between the month's end at 11 PM and the 1st's rollover; tests/remaining-09-banking.test.ts, the ING journey.

before: This card year began August 25, 2026, paid in advance with 950 kr, and runs to August 24, 2027. The next year is charged August 25, 2027. … Its days are counted by Reykjavík’s calendar. If the account can’t cover the year’s fee, it’s charged anyway, and the account goes below zero by the difference. Estimated: Arion’s price list and terms don’t say when in the year it’s charged.
after: The current card year runs from August 25, 2026 to August 24, 2027, and you paid 950 kr for it in advance. The next year’s fee is charged on August 25, 2027. … The bank counts the card year’s days by the date in Reykjavík. If the account can’t cover the fee, the bank charges it anyway and the account goes overdrawn by the difference. The timing is estimated: Arion’s price list and terms don’t say when in the year it’s charged.
why: The year as a span, the glossary's 'overdrawn', and the estimate label says what's estimated. Variant: 'and nothing was charged for it' under the age the bank spares.
